sections.title: The Seven Angels with the Seven Plagues
observations: This section introduces the seven angels who are given seven plagues, which are the final judgments of God upon the earth. The imagery of plagues evokes the judgments seen in the Exodus narrative, emphasizing God's sovereignty and justice.

The sea of glass mixed with fire symbolizes the purity and holiness of God, as well as the judgment that is about to be executed. It serves as a reminder of God's power over creation and His ability to deliver His people from oppression.

sections.title: The Song of Moses and the Lamb
observations: The song sung by the victorious saints reflects themes of God's greatness and His righteous acts. It draws parallels to the song of Moses in Exodus, highlighting the continuity of God's redemptive work throughout history.
This song emphasizes the attributes of God: His holiness, justice, and the ultimate victory of His people. It serves as a reminder that worship is a response to God's mighty deeds and character.

importantVerses.commentary: Great and amazing are your deeds, O Lord God the Almighty! Just and true are your ways, O King of the nations!
Who will not fear, O Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy. All nations will come and worship you, for your righteous acts have been revealed.

questions: What do the plagues signify in the context of God's judgment?
How does the imagery of the sea of glass contribute to our understanding of God's holiness?
In what ways does the song of Moses and the Lamb connect the Old Testament with the New Testament?
What does it mean for all nations to come and worship God, and how does this shape our understanding of God's plan for humanity?
